posts.text:
Speed to lead is real.

The odds of reaching a new lead drop hard after the first few minutes. Most small businesses reply in hours, if at all.

You don't need a bigger team to fix that. You need the first reply to go out on its own.

What happens to a new lead at your business in the first 5 minutes?

Most customers go with the business that gets back to them first.

If your lead form or missed call takes 2 hours to get a reply, you're not losing that job to a better competitor. You're handing it to a faster one.

How fast does your business reply to a new inquiry?

Comment your response time and I'll share the setup we use to reply in under a minute.

Your website has one job.

Not to look pretty. Not to win awards. To get the phone to ring.

If a stranger can't find your number and a reason to call within 5 seconds, it's failing that job.

Pull up your homepage. How long does it take to find your phone number?

This account runs on a schedule my AI keeps.

It drafts, checks and books the posts. Every reply you get from me is me, typed by hand.

That's the split I recommend to every owner. Let AI do the repeat work. Keep the human part human.

What's one repeat task you'd hand off first?

Owners, real talk.

What keeps a lead from turning into a paying job at your business?

A) Slow reply
B) Missed calls
C) Price shoppers
D) No follow up

Reply with your letter and I'll reply with a fix for yours.

Voicemail is where leads go to die.

Most callers who hit voicemail don't leave a message. They hang up and call the next name on Google.

If you can't pick up, something should.

When did you last check how many calls hung up on your voicemail?

Your business closes at 5 PM. Your customers' free time starts at 5 PM.

That's when they finally sit down and call about the leak, the roof, the quote they've been putting off.

An AI receptionist doesn't replace your team. It catches the $2,000 job that called while you were at dinner.

Drop your industry and I'll tell you the top reason callers hang up before leaving a voicemail.

Put your phone number in the top right corner of your website.

Make it a tap to call button on phones.

It sounds too simple to matter. It's one of the fastest wins on almost every local site.

Is your number tappable right now? Check on your phone.

Our own website has an AI chat assistant named Ava.

Someone asks a question at 2 AM, Ava answers it, collects their details, and the lead lands in our CRM and my inbox before I wake up.

No one waits until morning for a reply.

Would your customers use a chat like that, or do they only call?

Free thing for home service owners 👇

Our 5 Star Review Kit shows you how to get more Google reviews from the customers who already love you.

Grab it here
evogencyglobal.com/free-review-kit

An AI receptionist isn't a phone tree.

No "press 1 for sales." It talks like a person, answers common questions, and books the job right on your calendar.

The caller just thinks your office picked up fast.

Would your customers notice the difference?

3 things quietly killing your homepage.

1. Visitors can't tell what you do in 5 seconds
2. There's no clear button to call or book at the top of the page
3. It takes more than a couple of seconds to load on a phone

Fix these three and you'll see noticeably more calls and form fills.

Want an honest 60 second critique of your homepage? Leave your URL below.

Agents, your listing page is your best salesperson at midnight.

Big photos. The price up top. One button to book a showing.

If a buyer has to dig for any of those, they're back on Zillow.

What's the first thing buyers ask you about a listing?

Before I pitch a local business, I build them a free concept homepage.

Not a slideshow. A real page with their name, their services and a clear call button.

Owners don't buy promises. They buy what they can see.

Would you rather see a mockup or hear a pitch?

How do new customers find your business right now?

A) Google
B) Word of mouth
C) Social media
D) Honestly not sure

Reply with your letter. If it's D, that's the first thing worth fixing.

The most expensive phone call is the one you didn't answer.

You already paid for it. The ad, the truck wrap, the Google listing. All of it worked. The customer called.

Then nobody picked up.

Do you know how many calls you missed last month?

A website builder loaded with plugins you don't use is slowing you down.

Every extra script makes your site heavier on phones. Slower pages rank lower on Google, and if you run ads, you pay for clicks that leave before the page even loads.

Try this. Run your site through Google PageSpeed Insights right now.

What's your mobile score? Drop it below.

Stock photos are quietly costing you trust.

Customers can tell. A real photo of your crew, your truck or a finished job beats a smiling model every time.

One real photo on your homepage this week. That's the assignment.

What photo would you put up first?

We built our own CRM because nothing off the shelf fit how a small agency runs.

Every lead from the site, the chat and the phone lands in one place, with the next step attached.

No spreadsheets. No sticky notes.

Where do your leads live right now?

Want to know where your website is leaking calls?

Reply AUDIT and I'll look at it and send you the top 3 fixes. Free, no pitch.

I'm doing a few of these this week.

Things AI handles well for a small business today.

1. Answering the phone after hours
2. Replying to new leads in seconds
3. Sending appointment reminders
4. Asking happy customers for reviews

None of it replaces your team. All of it frees them up.

Which one would save you the most time?

Quick question for business owners.

What's the one task you or your team do by hand every single week that you wish would just happen on its own?

Describe it in one sentence below and I'll sketch out how to automate it in the replies.

A contact form with 12 fields is a polite way of saying go away.

Name, phone, what you need. That's enough to start.

Every extra field you add, fewer people finish.

How many fields is your contact form asking for?

We built a tool that turns a contractor's phone clips of a finished job into a short promo video.

Shoot the job on your phone. Get back a clip ready for Facebook and Instagram.

The best marketing a tradesman has is the work itself.

Do you film your finished jobs?

Quick gut check before the weekend.

If a customer called your business at 8 PM tonight, what would happen?

A) I'd pick up
B) Voicemail
C) It rings out
D) An answering service

Reply with your letter.

Saturday is a busy day for calls and a quiet day for offices.

That gap is where your competitors win jobs you never knew about.

Who's covering your phone this weekend?

How a good real estate team never loses a buyer lead 👇

1. A Zillow lead lands in the CRM
2. A text goes out to the buyer within seconds
3. A showing call gets booked automatically
4. The agent gets a ping with everything they need

No copy and paste. No lead sitting cold overnight.

Agents, are you still typing lead info into your CRM by hand?

If your website loads slowly on a phone, visitors leave before they ever see your offer.

Three quick fixes.

1. Shrink your images
2. Cut the plugins you don't use
3. Drop the autoplay video at the top

Which of these is your site guilty of?

Our outreach runs on an AI assistant that researches businesses and drafts the emails every night.

I read every draft and hit send myself.

AI does the digging. A human does the talking. That's how it should work.

Would you trust AI to write your emails, or just draft them?

Owners, what's the one tool your business can't live without?

Drop it below. I'm curious what's running Main Street right now.

A slow Sunday is the best time to test your lead flow.

Call your own business. Fill out your own contact form. Time how long the reply takes.

You'll learn more in 10 minutes than in a month of guessing.

What did you find?

Be honest.

How many calls did your business miss or send to voicemail this past week?

A) 0 to 5
B) 6 to 15
C) More than 15
D) I don't want to know

Reply with your letter. No judgment, most owners have never checked.

The best homepages answer three questions fast.

1. What do you do?
2. Where do you do it?
3. How do I reach you?

If yours answers all three before anyone scrolls, you're ahead of most local sites.

Does yours pass?

This week on here, we talked about missed calls, slow replies and websites that don't get the phone to ring.

Next week, I'm showing what fixing it looks like. Real builds doing real work.

What do you want to see first?

If this week hit a nerve, let's look at your setup together.

Reply AUDIT and I'll check your website and how your calls are handled, then send you the quick fixes.

Free. No pitch.
